Bug_Title: SING: Class using singleton design pattern has non-private constructor. (SING_SINGLETON_HAS_NONPRIVATE_CONSTRUCTOR)
Bug_Details:
This class is using singleton design pattern and has non-private constructor (please note that a default constructor might exist which is not private). Given that, it is possible to create a copy of the object, thus violating the singleton pattern.
The easier solution would be making the constructor private.
SEI CERT MSC07-J rule
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by having a public constructor in the SingletonExample class. This allows multiple instances of the class to be created, violating the singleton pattern.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the'showBug' method of the SingletonExample class, which attempts to create a new instance of the class using its public constructor. This triggers the bug because the constructor is not private, allowing multiple instances to be created.
